methods.text_lengths: Regex word counts, not model-tokenizer lengths.
methods.categorical_associations: Bias-corrected Cramer's V with expected-cell sparsity; descriptive, missing category included, no p-values.
methods.nutrition_numeric_states: Blank/null/none/NA-style tokens are missing; numeric NaN/infinity are nonfinite; invalid text and negatives are separate.
methods.nutrition_correlations: Pearson and average-tie-rank Spearman; pairwise finite nonnegative values; minimum 10 pairs; constant/insufficient pairs unavailable.
methods.population_inference: No causal, population-prevalence, real-athlete outcome, or measured-model-performance claims.
methods.figure_rendering: All charts regenerated from current verified inputs; DejaVu Sans, 160 dpi. Rendering can differ across software versions.

majority_reference.population: preliminary candidates with present source labels
majority_reference.evaluation_status: Full-catalog descriptive reference; no holdout predictions or measured model performance.

findings.observation: 1550 of 2909 exercises lack an available description.
findings.implication: Report text availability by label and assess name-only performance separately.
findings.limitation: A missing description is not evidence that an exercise is unusable or unsuitable for a particular athlete.

findings.observation: The two largest source-label categories account for 44.8608% of records; the largest/smallest ratio is 82.5.
findings.implication: Use per-class metrics and training-only balancing; examine distinct split-group support before final partitions.
findings.limitation: Source-label counts describe this collected catalog, not population exercise prevalence or validated muscle targeting.

findings.observation: 2581 split groups retain 2909 exercises, including 46 mixed-label groups.
findings.implication: Use group-aware partitioning and investigate label conflicts before freezing training targets.
findings.limitation: Similarity links are conservative split protection and do not establish canonical exercise identity or statistical independence.

findings.observation: The review queue contains 2333 entries; 2333 active entries remain unresolved across 2072 exercises.
findings.implication: Track review progress without treating overlapping findings as independent records or automatically excluding flagged examples.
findings.limitation: A preserved handling decision does not independently verify the original publisher label or youth suitability.

findings.observation: Categorical associations and cross-tabs describe the source labels, text availability, and catalog metadata.
findings.implication: Inspect uneven documentation and collection patterns while retaining the name-and-description feature contract.
findings.limitation: No p-values or causal claims are made; sparse categories and related records limit interpretation, and metadata association does not authorize new predictors.

findings.observation: 411 food records; 321 have finite core values and 313 have finite nonnegative core values.
findings.implication: Use explicit numeric eligibility masks and report the sample size for each comparison.
findings.limitation: Completeness and nonnegativity do not independently verify food identity, reference amount, or suitability for an individual athlete.

findings.observation: Energy and macronutrient associations were described using finite nonnegative pairs.
findings.implication: Interpret food-composition patterns in the context of the recorded energy convention.
findings.limitation: Derived food energy can be mathematically related to macronutrients; these are not independent athlete outcomes or evidence of benefit.

findings.implication: Use the separate sources to examine request and constraint coverage and identify missing planner inputs.
findings.limitation: Fictional development examples do not establish population prevalence, validated drill labels, or an independent final test set.

findings.observation: 23 imported activity occurrences form 22 normalized name groups and link to 23 derived RAG documents.
findings.implication: Review coaching coverage, identities, permissions, and requirements in Step 12; evaluate retrieval separately.
findings.limitation: Derived RAG documents are another representation of the same activities, not additional independent drills or source evidence. Historical catalog versions are not additive.

findings.observation: 5 guidance records and 17 structured reference rules were described.
findings.implication: Use Step 13 to reconcile population segments, evidence, and planning inputs before implementation.
findings.limitation: These are reference rules, not measured recovery outcomes. Recorded verification wording is not an individual prescription or approval by this analysis.

findings.observation: The verified Step 9 summary records 256337 master-index rows across 9 entity types.
findings.implication: Keep source domains separate and choose inputs according to each project component.
findings.limitation: Historical player records and nutrition tables do not supply validated youth drill-to-profile outcomes or a joint supervised target.

findings.observation: 9 historical inputs were absent from the checked Step 8 locations.
findings.implication: Retain the lineage limitation and resolve publisher inputs and permissions before release.
findings.limitation: This local analysis does not refresh publisher pages, validate source acquisition, or grant usage rights.
